paper.title_en: Sampling nucleon short-range correlations in coordinate and momentum space for Au+Au collision simulations
paper.abstract_en: We develop a nuclear initialization scheme that jointly incorporates spatial nucleon correlations, high-momentum components, predominantly proton-neutron pair assignments, and correlated pair momenta, and implement it in the SMASH transport model. This construction enables controlled comparisons of the effects of different ingredients of short-range correlations (SRCs) on heavy-ion observables. For Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.4$ GeV, SRC initialization increases both charged-pion yields relative to a Woods-Saxon reference with Fermi momenta when the same mean-field parameters are used. The larger relative enhancement of $π^+$ production reduces the $π^-/π^+$ ratio. Controlled comparisons identify the modified single-nucleon momentum distribution as the dominant source of the enhancement, with smaller effects from the tested spatial and pair-isospin variations and enhanced production persisting without the imposed pair-momentum structure. Reaction histories link this enhancement to increased baryon-resonance production. Stronger high-momentum repulsion counteracts the SRC-induced pion enhancement by reducing the energy available in nucleon-nucleon collisions and suppressing resonance production. The similar enhancement of $K^+$ production with SRC initialization and its reduction after refitting the mean-field parameters show that the competing effects of correlated initialization and mean-field dynamics extend beyond pion production.
